subject.title: Bug: preflight (budget-triggered) compaction hard-capped at ~60s, ignores compaction.timeoutSeconds

question: Should maintainers accept https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95590 as the canonical cancellation fix for this issue, require exact slow-backend proof first, or pursue a separate preflight config gate?
rationale: Current main and the latest release still show the bug, but the remaining choice affects session-state cancellation semantics and possibly new configuration surface, which should not be chosen by cleanup automation.

options.title: Land the filtered cancellation fix
options.body: Accept the open candidate PR's contract that lifecycle `TimeoutError` aborts should not cancel required preflight compaction while explicit and non-timeout aborts still do.

options.title: Require exact slow-backend proof
options.body: Keep the issue and candidate PR paused until a redacted run from the reporter's slow vLLM/Qwen-style setup proves the end-to-end duration behavior.

options.title: Split out the config gate
options.body: Resolve the abort-signal bug first and handle `compaction.preflight.enabled` as a separate product/config discussion.

recommendation.title: Land the filtered cancellation fix
recommendation.body: Accept the open candidate PR's contract that lifecycle `TimeoutError` aborts should not cancel required preflight compaction while explicit and non-timeout aborts still do.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision centers on reply lifecycle cancellation semantics, and the strongest feature-history signal for that contract is commit 3f6840230b86.
